beats: Same job, same forty-five thousand dollar salary. Nora gets a grocery benefit every quarter. Sam gets nothing. The CRA isn't looking at your salary.
Benefits like the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit use family net income: yours plus your spouse's.
Nora is single. Forty-five thousand is under forty-six thousand four hundred and thirty-two, so she gets the full six hundred and seventy-nine dollars.
Sam's partner earns thirty-five thousand. Family income: eighty thousand.
That's thirty-three thousand five hundred and sixty-eight over the line. Five percent of that wipes out the whole benefit. Zero.
The twist: sometimes it's not income at all. If either spouse didn't file a return, the payments stop.
So check your family net income, and make sure both of you filed.
